title: Texas's 10th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: Texas's 10th Congressional District is an open seat in 2026 as long-serving Republican incumbent Michael McCaul retires after more than two decades in Congress. The district, which stretches from northern Austin through the Brazos Valley to the outskirts of Houston, has a strong Republican lean (R+10) and voted for Donald Trump by 60% to 38% in 2024. Republican nominee Chris Gober, a prominent conservative attorney and former director of Elon Musk's America PAC who was endorsed by President Trump, won a crowded 10-candidate primary with 51% of the vote. He faces Democratic nominee Caitlin Rourk, a U.S. Army veteran and former Dell Technologies executive, in the general election, with the race viewed as likely Republican-held but drawing national attention due to the open seat dynamics.
polling_note: No district-specific general election polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. Generic ballot polls for Texas showed a narrow Republican advantage.

candidates.name: Chris Gober
candidates.summary: Chris Gober is a 7th-generation Texan, conservative attorney, and the Republican nominee for Texas's 10th Congressional District. He is the founding partner and CEO of Lex Politica, a national law firm focused on constitutional and political litigation, and previously served as director and chief lawyer for Elon Musk's America PAC. He has won major legal victories including a U.S. Supreme Court case for Senator Ted Cruz and a lawsuit striking down IRS regulations targeting conservative groups.

candidates.name: Caitlin Rourk
candidates.summary: Caitlin Rourk is a U.S. Army veteran, former Dell Technologies executive, and the Democratic nominee for Texas's 10th Congressional District. She earned her commission as a Military Intelligence Officer through Army Officer Candidate School and served in the Texas Army National Guard, supporting disaster response and border mobilizations. A Central Texan raised by public school teachers, she holds a BA from the University of Chicago and an MBA from the McCombs School of Business at the University of Texas at Austin.

forecast.rationale: This open-seat race in Texas's 10th Congressional District strongly favors Republicans based on structural fundamentals rather than polling (no district-specific general election polls exist). The district carries an R+10 partisan lean and voted for Donald Trump by a 60%-38% margin in 2024, providing a clear Republican baseline advantage of roughly 12-22 points. Republican nominee Chris Gober's strong primary performance (51% in a 10-candidate field) combined with his Trump endorsement, ties to conservative legal circles, and previous role directing Elon Musk's America PAC signal a well-positioned and well-funded campaign. Democratic nominee Caitlin Rourk is a credible candidate as an Army veteran and former Dell executive, but is running in difficult partisan territory. The open-seat dynamic introduces some additional uncertainty versus an incumbent-held race, and the complete absence of district-level polling prevents more precise calibration. Nonetheless, the available structural data points to a likely Republican hold in the 80-94% probability range.
